{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish, since its outline reads clearly, and sketched it on the pad with the body split into top, bottom and tail strokes. I laid the whole top line from the start to the tail point. When the tail stalled I took the fin myself, cleared the stray loop at the tail, and re-laid the fin. I also bridged the break in the bottom line just before the tail. At the final check about 109 of the 120 standing dominoes fall from the start, and the fall carries along both body lines and round the fin. I can't claim the judge recognised it, because that isn't known yet. The tail also came out as a rounded fin rather than the pointed one on the pad, so it is less crisp than planned. I'm hopeful it still reads as a fish.

Execution: Overall the build was solid. The top line, nose joins and bridge worked. There were misses. My first fin attempt ended up inside the loop, my first nudge on the bottom line placed nothing, and I had to switch to a proper join. A few stray dominoes remain unconnected near the bridge and tail. They don't change the outline, but they weren't fully cleaned up. I checked my own work and fixed what I found.

Collaboration: I gave each person a clear stroke or role and kept everyone updated on what I was touching. I stayed off Priya's bottom line and loop clearing and left the tail join to her, so we didn't undo each other's work. I also corrected my own assumption when Tom's hands weren't on the tail and reassigned the work. Maya's final run check and Priya's join work were important, and I made a point of staying off the build once it was verified.

Leadership: I set the direction early, split the work, and stepped in on the tail when it was the bottleneck. I kept the table focused on the remaining breaks rather than redoing things. Looking back, I could have checked the tail earlier against the pad and made sure Tom was engaged from the start."}
